title: Main axis and cross axis
learningObjectives: Explain main axis and cross axis and build a practical layout with it.

understand.concept: Flexbox uses a main axis and a cross axis. flex-direction determines the main axis: row follows the inline direction, while column follows the block direction in the relevant writing mode. Alignment properties operate relative to these axes.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding axes prevents confusion between justify-content and align-items. The axes change when flex-direction changes and can be affected by writing mode and direction.
understand.analogy: Imagine a line of items: the main axis follows the line; the cross axis runs across it.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual flex layout follows the flex formatting algorithm and writing-mode rules.

explain.narrative: The first group has a horizontal main axis; the second has a vertical main axis.

examples.explanation: The first group has a horizontal main axis; the second has a vertical main axis.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered demonstration of the layout concept.

practise.guidedTask: Change row to row-reverse and column to column-reverse. Describe how the main axis and item order change.
practise.independentTask: Build a responsive component using this concept. Test long labels, narrow widths, and keyboard navigation.
hints: Inspect the flex container and items in developer tools.
Change one axis or alignment property at a time.
Test with translated or longer labels.
